fixes.explanation: Nice try, friend, but nobody is giving a speech in this verse. The text says he bows in worship at the threshold of the gate and then departs. No scroll, no microphone, just a bow, and then he's out the door.

East gate?! Friend, I love the confidence, I do. But this verse only talks about the north and south gates, and the worshiper who enters by the north gate must go out by the south gate. No one is to return through the gate by which he entered, so no turning around. It's a one-way aisle, so keep it moving.

Ha, I get the doubt, friend, but this one is true. The text says that when the prince makes a freewill offering, the gate facing east must be opened for him. After he goes out, the gate must be closed. That's one gate with very clear working hours.

Brothers? Good guess, friend, but not a single crumb of this verse goes to them. The text says the gift to a son will belong to his descendants. It becomes their property by inheritance, so it keeps rolling down the family line.

The priests are waiting by the door for that gift, friend, but it never shows up. A gift to a servant belongs to that servant until the year of freedom. Then it reverts to the prince. Back to the prince, no detours.

Gatekeepers bunking in the kitchen? That's a lot of noise for a good night's sleep, friend. The man says it's where the priests shall boil the guilt offering and the sin offering. They also bake the grain offering there, so it's a kitchen, not a bunkhouse.

Plot twist, friend, that one is true. The man says the priests boil and bake there “…so that they do not bring them into the outer court and transmit holiness to the people.” The cooking stays at the far western end of the priests' holy chambers, and the outer court stays out of it. That's a kitchen with a very clear boundary.
